exam: JLPT N5 (日本語能力試験 N5)
description: Japanese Language Proficiency Test – Level N5. Covers basic vocabulary, kanji, grammar, and reading comprehension.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 「水」(みず)?
questions.explanation: 水 (みず / mizu) means 'water'. It is one of the most basic kanji taught at N5 level.

questions.question: What does 「学校」(がっこう) mean?
questions.explanation: 学校 (がっこう / gakkou) means 'school'. 学 = study/learning, 校 = institution.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 「先生」(せんせい)?
questions.explanation: 先生 (せんせい / sensei) means 'teacher' or 'instructor'. It is also used as an honorific for doctors and lawyers.

questions.question: What does 「電車」(でんしゃ) mean?
questions.explanation: 電車 (でんしゃ / densha) means 'electric train'. 電 = electricity, 車 = vehicle/car.

questions.question: What is 「本」(ほん)?
questions.explanation: 本 (ほん / hon) means 'book'. It also means 'origin' or 'true', but in everyday context it usually refers to a book.

questions.question: What does 「友達」(ともだち) mean?
questions.explanation: 友達 (ともだち / tomodachi) means 'friend'. 友 = friend, 達 = pluralizing suffix for people.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 「山」(やま)?
questions.explanation: 山 (やま / yama) means 'mountain'. It is a very common N5 kanji.

questions.question: What does 「犬」(いぬ) mean?
questions.explanation: 犬 (いぬ / inu) means 'dog'. Compare with 猫 (ねこ / neko) which means 'cat'.

questions.question: What is 「食べ物」(たべもの)?
questions.explanation: 食べ物 (たべもの / tabemono) means 'food'. 食べる = to eat, 物 = thing/object.

questions.question: What does 「時間」(じかん) mean?
questions.explanation: 時間 (じかん / jikan) means 'time' or 'hour'. 時 = time/hour, 間 = interval/space.

questions.question: What is 「駅」(えき)?
questions.explanation: 駅 (えき / eki) means 'train station'. It specifically refers to railway/subway stations.

questions.question: What does 「お金」(おかね) mean?
questions.explanation: お金 (おかね / okane) means 'money'. The お is an honorific prefix. 金 alone means 'gold' or 'money'.

questions.question: What is 「天気」(てんき)?
questions.explanation: 天気 (てんき / tenki) means 'weather'. 天 = sky/heaven, 気 = spirit/air/feeling.

questions.question: What does 「家族」(かぞく) mean?
questions.explanation: 家族 (かぞく / kazoku) means 'family'. 家 = house/home, 族 = family/tribe.

questions.question: What is 「病院」(びょういん)?
questions.explanation: 病院 (びょういん / byouin) means 'hospital'. 病 = illness, 院 = institution/hall.

questions.question: What does the verb 「食べる」(たべる) mean?
questions.explanation: 食べる (たべる / taberu) means 'to eat'. It is a Group 2 (ichidan) verb.

questions.question: What does 「飲む」(のむ) mean?
questions.explanation: 飲む (のむ / nomu) means 'to drink'. It is a Group 1 (godan) verb ending in む.

questions.question: What does 「行く」(いく) mean?
questions.explanation: 行く (いく / iku) means 'to go'. It is a Group 1 (godan) verb. Compare with 来る (くる) = to come.

questions.question: What does 「見る」(みる) mean?
questions.explanation: 見る (みる / miru) means 'to see' or 'to watch'. It is a Group 2 (ichidan) verb.

questions.question: What does 「書く」(かく) mean?
questions.explanation: 書く (かく / kaku) means 'to write'. Note: 描く (かく) can also mean 'to draw', but in N5 context 書く = write.

questions.question: What does 「聞く」(きく) mean?
questions.explanation: 聞く (きく / kiku) means both 'to listen' and 'to ask'. Context determines the meaning.

questions.question: What does 「来る」(くる) mean?
questions.explanation: 来る (くる / kuru) means 'to come'. It is an irregular verb (Group 3), along with する (to do).

questions.question: What does 「寝る」(ねる) mean?
questions.explanation: 寝る (ねる / neru) means 'to sleep' or 'to go to bed'. It is a Group 2 (ichidan) verb.

questions.question: What does 「起きる」(おきる) mean?
questions.explanation: 起きる (おきる / okiru) means 'to wake up' or 'to get up'. It is a Group 2 (ichidan) verb.

questions.question: What does 「買う」(かう) mean?
questions.explanation: 買う (かう / kau) means 'to buy'. It is a Group 1 (godan) verb. The opposite is 売る (うる) = to sell.

questions.question: What does 「大きい」(おおきい) mean?
questions.explanation: 大きい (おおきい / ookii) means 'big' or 'large'. It is an i-adjective. The opposite is 小さい (ちいさい) = small.

questions.question: What does 「新しい」(あたらしい) mean?
questions.explanation: 新しい (あたらしい / atarashii) means 'new'. The opposite is 古い (ふるい / furui) = old.

questions.question: What does 「高い」(たかい) mean?
questions.explanation: 高い (たかい / takai) means 'expensive', 'high', or 'tall' depending on context. The opposite for price is 安い (やすい) = cheap.

questions.question: What does 「好き」(すき) mean?
questions.explanation: 好き (すき / suki) is a na-adjective meaning 'to like' or 'to be fond of'. The opposite is 嫌い (きらい / kirai) = to dislike.

questions.question: What does 「難しい」(むずかしい) mean?
questions.explanation: 難しい (むずかしい / muzukashii) means 'difficult'. The opposite is 易しい (やさしい) = easy (or kind).

questions.question: What does 「楽しい」(たのしい) mean?
questions.explanation: 楽しい (たのしい / tanoshii) means 'fun' or 'enjoyable'. Related: 楽しむ (to enjoy).

questions.question: How do you say '7' in Japanese?
questions.explanation: 7 can be read as しち (shichi) or なな (nana). Both are correct. なな is more commonly used to avoid confusion with いち (1).

questions.question: What number is 「百」(ひゃく)?
questions.explanation: 百 (ひゃく / hyaku) = 100. 千 (せん / sen) = 1,000. 万 (まん / man) = 10,000.

questions.question: What does 「今日」(きょう) mean?
questions.explanation: 今日 (きょう / kyou) means 'today'. 昨日 (きのう) = yesterday, 明日 (あした) = tomorrow.

questions.question: What does 「毎日」(まいにち) mean?
questions.explanation: 毎日 (まいにち / mainichi) means 'every day'. 毎 = every. 毎週 = every week, 毎月 = every month.

questions.question: What does 「右」(みぎ) mean?
questions.explanation: 右 (みぎ / migi) means 'right'. 左 (ひだり / hidari) = left.

questions.question: What does 「上」(うえ) mean?
questions.explanation: 上 (うえ / ue) means 'above', 'on top', or 'up'. 下 (した / shita) = below/under.

questions.question: What color is 「赤」(あか)?
questions.explanation: 赤 (あか / aka) means 'red'. 青 (あお) = blue/green, 黄色 (きいろ) = yellow, 白 (しろ) = white, 黒 (くろ) = black.

questions.question: What color is 「白」(しろ)?
questions.explanation: 白 (しろ / shiro) means 'white'. 黒 (くろ / kuro) = black.

questions.question: What does 「目」(め) mean?
questions.explanation: 目 (め / me) means 'eye'. 耳 (みみ) = ear, 鼻 (はな) = nose, 口 (くち) = mouth.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「火曜日」?
questions.explanation: 火曜日 (かようび / kayoubi) means 'Tuesday'. 火 = fire. Days: 月(Mon)火(Tue)水(Wed)木(Thu)金(Fri)土(Sat)日(Sun).

questions.question: What is the reading of 「月曜日」?
questions.explanation: 月曜日 (げつようび / getsuyoubi) means 'Monday'. 月 = moon/month.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「何時」?
questions.explanation: 何時 (なんじ / nanji) means 'what time?' 何 = what/how many, 時 = o'clock/time.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「入口」?
questions.explanation: 入口 (いりぐち / iriguchi) means 'entrance'. 入 = enter, 口 = mouth/opening. Exit = 出口 (でぐち).

questions.question: What is the reading of 「外国人」?
questions.explanation: 外国人 (がいこくじん / gaikokujin) means 'foreigner'. 外 = outside, 国 = country, 人 = person.

questions.question: Which kanji means 'river'?
questions.explanation: 川 (かわ / kawa) means 'river'. 山 = mountain, 海 = sea, 池 = pond.

questions.question: Which kanji means 'person'?
questions.explanation: 人 (ひと / hito, じん / jin, にん / nin) means 'person'. One of the most fundamental kanji.

questions.question: Which kanji means 'sun' or 'day'?
questions.explanation: 日 (ひ / hi, にち / nichi, か / ka) means 'sun', 'day', or 'Japan'. 月 = moon/month.

questions.question: Which kanji means 'tree' or 'wood'?
questions.explanation: 木 (き / ki, もく / moku) means 'tree' or 'wood'. Also used for Thursday (木曜日).

questions.question: Which kanji means 'mouth'?
questions.explanation: 口 (くち / kuchi) means 'mouth'. Also used in words like 入口 (entrance) and 出口 (exit).

questions.question: Which kanji means 'electricity' or 'electric'?
questions.explanation: 電 (でん / den) means 'electricity'. Seen in 電車 (train), 電話 (telephone), 電気 (electricity/light).

questions.question: Which kanji means 'middle' or 'inside'?
questions.explanation: 中 (なか / naka, ちゅう / chuu) means 'middle', 'inside', or 'during'. Also means 'China' in 中国.

questions.question: Which kanji represents 'woman'?
questions.explanation: 女 (おんな / onna) means 'woman' or 'female'. 男 (おとこ) = man/male.

questions.question: What does the kanji 「半」mean?
questions.explanation: 半 (はん / han) means 'half'. Used in time expressions: 三時半 (さんじはん) = 3:30.

questions.question: What does 「日本語」(にほんご) mean?
questions.explanation: 日本語 (にほんご / nihongo) = Japanese language. 日本 = Japan, 語 = language.

questions.question: What does 「大学」(だいがく) mean?
questions.explanation: 大学 (だいがく / daigaku) = university/college. 大 = big/great, 学 = learning/study.

questions.question: What does 「出口」(でぐち) mean?
questions.explanation: 出口 (でぐち / deguchi) = exit. 出 = go out, 口 = opening/mouth. Entrance = 入口 (いりぐち).

questions.question: What does 「電話」(でんわ) mean?
questions.explanation: 電話 (でんわ / denwa) = telephone. 電 = electric, 話 = speech/talk.

questions.question: What does 「毎朝」(まいあさ) mean?
questions.explanation: 毎朝 (まいあさ / maiasa) = every morning. 毎 = every, 朝 = morning.

questions.question: What does 「何人」(なんにん) mean?
questions.explanation: 何人 (なんにん / nannin) = how many people? 何 = what/how many, 人 = person.

questions.question: Choose the correct particle: 私___学生です。(I am a student.)
questions.explanation: は (wa) is the topic marker particle. 私は学生です = 'As for me, I am a student.' This is the standard sentence pattern for identifying what something is.

questions.question: Choose the correct particle: 学校___行きます。(I go to school.)
questions.explanation: に (ni) marks a destination when used with movement verbs like 行く (go), 来る (come), 帰る (return). 学校に行きます = go to school.

questions.question: Choose the correct particle: バス___来ました。(I came by bus.)
questions.explanation: で (de) marks the means of transportation. バスで = by bus. Also used for location of action: 図書館で読む = read at the library.

questions.question: Choose the correct particle: 水___飲みます。(I drink water.)
questions.explanation: を (wo/o) marks the direct object of a transitive verb. 水を飲みます = drink water.

questions.question: Choose the correct particle: 東京___来ました。(I came from Tokyo.)
questions.explanation: から (kara) means 'from' and marks the starting point. 東京から = from Tokyo. まで = until/to (endpoint).

questions.question: Choose the correct particle: 机の上___本があります。(There is a book on the desk.)
questions.explanation: に (ni) marks existence location with あります/います. 机の上に本があります = there is a book on the desk.

questions.question: Choose the correct particle: 図書館___本を読みます。(I read books at the library.)
questions.explanation: で (de) marks the location where an action takes place. 図書館で = at the library (place of action). に is for existence/destination.

questions.question: Choose the correct particle: 猫___犬___好きです。(I like cats and dogs.)
questions.explanation: 猫と犬も好きです. と connects nouns exhaustively (A and B). も adds 'also'. Together: 'I like cats, and dogs too.'

questions.question: What is the negative form of 「食べます」?
questions.explanation: 食べます (tabemasu) → 食べません (tabemasen) is the polite negative present/future form. ～ません is the standard polite negative ending.

questions.question: What is the past tense of 「行きます」?
questions.explanation: 行きます (ikimasu) → 行きました (ikimashita) is the polite past affirmative form. ～ました is the standard polite past ending.

questions.question: What is the polite negative past form of 「来ます」?
questions.explanation: 来ます (kimasu) → 来ませんでした (kimasen deshita) = did not come. The polite negative past adds でした to the negative ません form.

questions.question: What is the て-form of 「食べる」?
questions.explanation: 食べる (ichidan/Group 2 verb) → て-form is 食べて. For ichidan verbs, remove る and add て. て-form is used for linking actions, requesting, and progressive aspect.

questions.question: What is the て-form of 「飲む」?
questions.explanation: 飲む (nomu) is a godan verb ending in む. The て-form rule: む → んで. So 飲む → 飲んで (nonde).

questions.question: What is the て-form of 「書く」?
questions.explanation: 書く (kaku) ends in く. The て-form rule: く → いて. So 書く → 書いて (kaite). Exception: 行く → 行って (not 行いて).

questions.question: What does 「～たい」express?
questions.explanation: ～たい (tai) expresses the speaker's desire to do something. 食べたい = want to eat. Attach to the verb stem (ます-form without ます).

questions.question: What does 「～てください」express?
questions.explanation: ～てください (te kudasai) is a polite request form. 見てください = please look/watch. It uses the て-form + ください.

questions.question: What does 「～ています」express?
questions.explanation: ～ています (te imasu) expresses a continuous/ongoing action or resultant state. 食べています = is eating. 結婚しています = is married (resultant state).

questions.question: What does 「～ないでください」express?
questions.explanation: ～ないでください (naide kudasai) is a polite negative request: 'please don't do ~'. 食べないでください = please don't eat.

questions.question: What does 「～ことができます」express?
questions.explanation: ～ことができます (koto ga dekimasu) expresses ability. 日本語を話すことができます = I can speak Japanese. The dictionary form precedes ことができます.

questions.question: How do you conjugate the i-adjective 「大きい」into its negative form?
questions.explanation: For i-adjectives, the negative form replaces い with くない. 大きい → 大きくない = not big. Exception: いい (good) → よくない (not good).

questions.question: How do you conjugate the na-adjective 「静か」(quiet) into its negative form?
questions.explanation: Na-adjectives use じゃない or ではない for the negative. 静かではない / 静かじゃない = not quiet. They behave more like nouns grammatically.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 私は学生___、田中さんは先生です。(I am a student, and Mr. Tanaka is a teacher.)
questions.explanation: The て-form of だ (the copula) is で. When listing two facts using nouns, use Noun + で to connect them. 学生で = being a student, and...

questions.question: Which sentence correctly expresses 'There are three cats here'?
options: ここに猫が三匹あります。
ここに猫が三匹います。
ここで猫が三匹います。
ここは猫が三匹あります。
questions.answer: ここに猫が三匹います。
questions.explanation: います is used for animate beings (people, animals). あります is for inanimate objects. 三匹 (さんびき) is the counter for small animals. Location uses に.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly says 'I like sushi'?
questions.explanation: 好き (like) and 嫌い (dislike) take が, not を, for the thing liked/disliked. Pattern: [Topic]は [object]が好きです.

questions.question: What does 「～から」mean at the end of a reason clause?
questions.explanation: から (kara) as a sentence-final conjunction means 'because'. 雨が降っているから、家にいます = Because it's raining, I'm staying home. Note: ので is a softer/more formal alternative.

questions.question: What does 「～が、～」mean as a conjunction?
questions.explanation: が (ga) used as a conjunction between clauses means 'but' or 'however'. 行きたいですが、時間がありません = I want to go, but I don't have time.

questions.question: What does 「どこ」mean?
questions.explanation: どこ (doko) = where. Other question words: 何 (なに) = what, 誰 (だれ) = who, いつ = when, どれ = which, どう/どんな = how/what kind.

questions.question: What does 「いくら」mean?
questions.explanation: いくら (ikura) = how much (price). いくつ = how many (for things/age). どのくらい = how much/how long (general).

questions.question: Which counter is used for long, thin objects like pencils and umbrellas?
questions.explanation: 本 (ほん) is the counter for long, cylindrical objects: pens, bottles, trees, rivers. 枚 = flat things, 冊 = bound books, 台 = machines/vehicles.

questions.question: Which counter is used for flat objects like paper and stamps?
questions.explanation: 枚 (まい) counts flat things: paper, stamps, tickets, T-shirts, plates. 一枚 (いちまい), 二枚 (にまい), 三枚 (さんまい)...

questions.question: Which counter is used for small animals?
questions.explanation: 匹 (ひき) counts small animals like cats, dogs, fish. 頭 (とう) = large animals (horses, cows). 羽 (わ) = birds. 一匹 (いっぴき), 二匹 (にひき).

questions.question: What is the past affirmative form of 「です」?
questions.explanation: です (desu) = is/am/are (present). でした (deshita) = was/were (past affirmative). じゃありませんでした = was not (past negative).

questions.question: What is the polite negative form of 「です」?
options: じゃないです / ではありません
questions.answer: じゃないです / ではありません
questions.explanation: The polite negative is じゃないです (informal) or ではありません (formal). 学生ではありません = I am not a student.

questions.question: What does 「～でしょう」express?
questions.explanation: でしょう (deshou) expresses probability or polite supposition. 明日は雨でしょう = It will probably rain tomorrow. Also used to seek agreement: そうでしょう?

questions.question: What does 「～てもいいですか」express?
questions.explanation: ～てもいいですか (te mo ii desu ka) = May I ~? / Is it okay if I ~? It asks for permission. てもいいです = you may / it's okay to.

questions.question: 「三時に会いましょう」means:
questions.explanation: 三時に (sanji ni) = at 3 o'clock. に marks a specific point in time. 会いましょう (aimashou) = let's meet (volitional form).

questions.question: Which sentence correctly expresses 'A is more [adjective] than B'?
questions.explanation: The comparison pattern is AはBより～です. より (yori) = than. 東京は大阪より大きいです = Tokyo is bigger than Osaka.

questions.question: How do you ask 'Which is more __ , A or B?' in Japanese?
questions.explanation: AとBとどちらが～ですか = Which is more ~, A or B? どちら = which of two. 犬と猫とどちらが好きですか = Which do you like better, dogs or cats?

questions.question: What does 「の」do in 「田中さんの本」?
questions.explanation: の (no) connects nouns to show possession or relationship. 田中さんの本 = Mr. Tanaka's book. It can also connect descriptive nouns: 日本語の先生 = Japanese language teacher.

questions.question: Which verb is used for the existence of inanimate objects?
questions.explanation: あります (arimasu) = there is / to exist / to have — used for inanimate objects. います (imasu) = used for animate beings (people, animals).

questions.passage: わたしはまいあさ七時におきます。そして、シャワーをあびて、朝ごはんを食べます。学校は八時半にはじまりますから、八時に家をでます。
questions.question: What time does this person wake up?
questions.explanation: まいあさ七時におきます = I wake up at 7:00 every morning. 七時 (しちじ) = 7 o'clock.

questions.passage: わたしはまいあさ七時におきます。そして、シャワーをあびて、朝ごはんを食べます。学校は八時半にはじまりますから、八時に家をでます。
questions.question: What time does school start?
questions.explanation: 学校は八時半にはじまります = School starts at 8:30. 八時半 (はちじはん) = 8:30.

questions.passage: きのうはとてもいい天気でした。だから、友達と公園でサッカーをしました。とても楽しかったです。でも、今日はあめです。
questions.question: What did this person do yesterday?
options: Played soccer at the park with a friend
questions.answer: Played soccer at the park with a friend
questions.explanation: 友達と公園でサッカーをしました = played soccer at the park with a friend. 友達 = friend, 公園 = park, サッカー = soccer.

questions.passage: きのうはとてもいい天気でした。だから、友達と公園でサッカーをしました。とても楽しかったです。でも、今日はあめです。
questions.question: What is the weather like today?
questions.explanation: 今日はあめです = Today it is rainy. あめ (雨) = rain.

questions.question: A sign reads「立入禁止」(たちいりきんし). What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 立入禁止 (たちいりきんし) = No entry / Keep out. 立入 = entering on foot, 禁止 = prohibited.

questions.question: A sign reads「禁煙」(きんえん). What does it mean?
questions.explanation: 禁煙 (きんえん) = No smoking. 禁 = forbidden, 煙 = smoke.

questions.passage: 図書館は月曜日から土曜日まで、午前九時から午後六時まで開いています。日曜日は休みです。
questions.question: When is the library closed?
questions.explanation: 日曜日は休みです = Sunday is a day off (closed). 月曜日から土曜日まで = from Monday to Saturday.

questions.passage: 図書館は月曜日から土曜日まで、午前九時から午後六時まで開いています。日曜日は休みです。
questions.question: What time does the library open?
questions.explanation: 午前九時から = from 9:00 AM. 午前 = AM (morning), 午後 = PM (afternoon).

questions.passage: たなかさんは会社員です。まいにち電車で会社にいきます。会社は東京にあります。たなかさんのうちは横浜にあります。
questions.question: Where is Mr. Tanaka's company?
questions.explanation: 会社は東京にあります = The company is in Tokyo.

questions.passage: たなかさんは会社員です。まいにち電車で会社にいきます。会社は東京にあります。たなかさんのうちは横浜にあります。
questions.question: How does Mr. Tanaka commute?
questions.explanation: まいにち電車で会社にいきます = goes to the company by train every day. 電車で = by train.

questions.question: What is the hiragana for the sound 'ka'?
questions.explanation: か = ka. The ka-row: か(ka) き(ki) く(ku) け(ke) こ(ko).

questions.question: What sound does 「ん」represent?
options: All of the above depending on context
questions.answer: All of the above depending on context
questions.explanation: ん is the moraic nasal. It sounds like 'n' before vowels/nasal consonants, 'm' before bilabial consonants, 'ng' before velar consonants. Never appears at the start of a word.

questions.question: What is the katakana for 'su'?
questions.explanation: ス = su. The sa-row in katakana: サ(sa) シ(shi) ス(su) セ(se) ソ(so).

questions.question: What word does 「テレビ」represent?
questions.explanation: テレビ = terebi = television (from English 'TV'). Katakana is commonly used for foreign loanwords.

questions.question: What word does 「コーヒー」represent?
questions.explanation: コーヒー (kōhī) = coffee. The ー represents a long vowel. This is an English loanword written in katakana.

questions.question: What word does 「アイスクリーム」represent?
questions.explanation: アイスクリーム (aisu kurīmu) = ice cream. From English 'ice cream', written in katakana as a loanword.

questions.question: What word does 「レストラン」represent?
questions.explanation: レストラン (resutoran) = restaurant. From French 'restaurant'. Katakana is used for foreign loanwords from all languages.

questions.question: You enter a shop and the staff says「いらっしゃいませ」. What does this mean?
questions.explanation: いらっしゃいませ is a formal/honorific welcome used by shop staff and hospitality workers. It is the imperative form of いらっしゃる (the honorific form of いる/来る/行く).

questions.question: Someone says「お先に失礼します」(おさきにしつれいします) before leaving the office. What do they mean?
options: Excuse me for leaving before you
Thank you for your hard work
questions.answer: Excuse me for leaving before you
questions.explanation: お先に失礼します is a standard phrase used when leaving the office before your colleagues. お先に = before you, 失礼します = excuse me/I'm being rude. The response is often お疲れ様です.

questions.question: Before eating a meal, Japanese people say「いただきます」. What does this express?
options: A humble expression of gratitude before receiving/eating
questions.answer: A humble expression of gratitude before receiving/eating
questions.explanation: いただきます (itadakimasu) literally means 'I humbly receive'. It is said before meals to express gratitude to those who prepared the food, and to nature/animals.

questions.question: What does 「すみません」mean?
questions.explanation: すみません (sumimasen) is used to get someone's attention ('excuse me'), apologize mildly, or express gratitude for a favor. For a deeper apology, use 申し訳ありません (moushiwake arimasen).

questions.question: What does 「ちょっと待ってください」mean?
questions.explanation: ちょっと待ってください (chotto matte kudasai) = please wait a moment. ちょっと = a little/a moment, 待って = wait (て-form of 待つ), ください = please.

questions.question: What does 「わかりません」mean?
options: I don't understand / I don't know
questions.answer: I don't understand / I don't know
questions.explanation: わかりません (wakarimasen) = I don't understand / I don't know. It's the polite negative of わかる (wakaru) = to understand.

questions.question: What does 「もう一度言ってください」mean?
options: Please say it one more time
questions.answer: Please say it one more time
questions.explanation: もう一度言ってください (mou ichido itte kudasai) = please say it one more time. もう = already/more, 一度 = once/one time, 言って = say (て-form).

questions.question: What is 「春」(はる)?
questions.explanation: 春 (はる / haru) = spring. 夏 (なつ) = summer, 秋 (あき) = autumn, 冬 (ふゆ) = winter.

questions.question: What is 「ご飯」(ごはん)?
questions.explanation: ご飯 (ごはん / gohan) = cooked rice, or a meal in general. 朝ご飯 = breakfast, 昼ご飯 = lunch, 夕ご飯 = dinner.

questions.question: What is 「郵便局」(ゆうびんきょく)?
questions.explanation: 郵便局 (ゆうびんきょく / yuubinkyoku) = post office. 郵便 = mail/post, 局 = bureau/office.

questions.question: What is 「スーパー」?
questions.explanation: スーパー (sūpā) = supermarket (from English 'super/supermarket'). コンビニ = convenience store, デパート = department store.

questions.question: What is 「服」(ふく)?
questions.explanation: 服 (ふく / fuku) = clothes/clothing. 靴 (くつ) = shoes, 帽子 (ぼうし) = hat, かばん = bag.

questions.question: What is 「雪」(ゆき)?
questions.explanation: 雪 (ゆき / yuki) = snow. 雨 (あめ) = rain, 風 (かぜ) = wind, 曇り (くもり) = cloudy.

questions.question: What is 「宿題」(しゅくだい)?
questions.explanation: 宿題 (しゅくだい / shukudai) = homework. 試験 (しけん) = exam, 授業 (じゅぎょう) = class/lesson.

questions.question: What is 「飛行機」(ひこうき)?
questions.explanation: 飛行機 (ひこうき / hikouki) = airplane. 飛 = fly, 行 = go, 機 = machine.

questions.question: What does 「熱」(ねつ) mean in the expression「熱があります」?
questions.explanation: 熱があります (netsu ga arimasu) = I have a fever. 熱 = heat/fever. 頭が痛い = headache, お腹が痛い = stomachache.

questions.question: How do you ask someone's age politely?
options: 何歳ですか / おいくつですか
questions.answer: 何歳ですか / おいくつですか
questions.explanation: 何歳ですか (nansai desu ka) = How old are you? おいくつですか is the polite version. Age counter: 〜歳 (さい).

questions.question: What is the word for 'older brother' (someone else's)?
questions.explanation: おにいさん (お兄さん) is used to refer to someone else's older brother. あに (兄) is used to refer to your own older brother humbly. This in-group/out-group distinction is key in Japanese.

questions.question: What is 「母」(はは)?
questions.explanation: 母 (はは / haha) = my own mother (in-group, humble form). お母さん (おかあさん) = someone else's mother or used to address your own mother directly.

questions.question: What does 「暑い」(あつい) mean?
questions.explanation: 暑い (あつい) = hot (weather/air temperature). 熱い (あつい) = hot (objects/food). 寒い (さむい) = cold (weather). 冷たい (つめたい) = cold (to the touch).

questions.question: Order these from most to least frequent: 「ときどき」「いつも」「たまに」「よく」
options: いつも > よく > ときどき > たまに
よく > いつも > たまに > ときどき
いつも > ときどき > よく > たまに
たまに > ときどき > よく > いつも
questions.answer: いつも > よく > ときどき > たまに
questions.explanation: いつも (always) > よく (often) > ときどき (sometimes) > たまに (rarely/occasionally). These are frequency adverbs important for N5.

questions.question: What does 「わかる」mean?
questions.explanation: わかる (wakaru) = to understand, to know. Note: it takes が, not を. 日本語がわかります = I understand Japanese.

questions.question: What does 「もらう」mean?
questions.explanation: もらう (morau) = to receive/get (from someone). あげる = to give (to someone). もらう is from the receiver's perspective.

questions.question: 「東京まで何時間かかりますか」– What does 「まで」indicate here?
questions.explanation: まで (made) marks the endpoint of movement or time. 東京まで = until/as far as Tokyo. から (from) + まで (to/until) often appear together.

questions.question: Which particle indicates the subject of a sentence, especially for new information or contrast?
questions.explanation: が (ga) marks the grammatical subject, especially for new information, answers to 'who/what' questions, and in subordinate clauses. は (wa) marks the topic (known information or contrast).

questions.question: What does 「～なければなりません」express?
questions.explanation: ～なければなりません (nakereba narimasen) = must do ~ / have to do ~. It expresses obligation. 宿題をしなければなりません = I must do my homework.

questions.question: What does 「～てはいけません」express?
questions.explanation: ～てはいけません (te wa ikemasen) = must not / not allowed to. 煙草を吸ってはいけません = You must not smoke. The opposite (permission) is ～てもいいです.

questions.question: The sentence 「映画を見たことがあります」means:
options: I want to see a movie
questions.explanation: ～たことがあります (ta koto ga arimasu) expresses past experience: 'have done ~'. 映画を見たことがあります = I have seen a movie (at least once).

questions.question: What does 「～つもりです」express?
questions.explanation: ～つもりです (tsumori desu) = intend to / plan to. 来年日本に行くつもりです = I intend to go to Japan next year. Uses the dictionary form of the verb.

questions.question: 「あまり～ません」means:
questions.explanation: あまり (amari) + negative = not very much / not often. 野菜をあまり食べません = I don't eat vegetables very much. あまり must be used with a negative verb.

questions.question: 「全然～ません」means:
questions.explanation: 全然 (ぜんぜん / zenzen) + negative = not at all. 日本語が全然わかりません = I don't understand Japanese at all. Like あまり, it must be paired with a negative.

questions.question: Fill the blank: 日本語は英語___難しいです。(Japanese is more difficult than English.)
questions.explanation: より (yori) = than. In comparisons: AはBより ～ = A is more ~ than B. 日本語は英語より難しいです = Japanese is more difficult than English.

questions.question: 「子供の時、よく公園で遊びました」means:
options: When I was a child, I often played at the park
When I was a child, I rarely went to the park
I will often play at the park when I have children
The children often play at the park
questions.answer: When I was a child, I often played at the park
questions.explanation: 子供の時 = when I was a child, よく = often, 公園で = at the park, 遊びました = played. Past tense of 遊ぶ (to play).

questions.question: What is the past tense of the i-adjective 「おいしい」(delicious)?
questions.explanation: I-adjective past tense: replace い with かった. おいしい → おいしかったです = was delicious. Polite form adds です.

questions.question: What is the adverbial form of 「速い」(fast)?
questions.explanation: I-adjectives become adverbs by replacing い with く. 速い (fast/quick) → 速く (quickly/fast). 速く走ります = runs fast.

questions.question: What is the adverbial form of 「静か」(quiet, na-adjective)?
questions.explanation: Na-adjectives become adverbs by adding に. 静か → 静かに (quietly). 静かに話してください = please speak quietly.

questions.question: Which verb is used when giving something to someone of equal or lower status?
questions.explanation: あげる (ageru) = to give (from you/your side to others). くれる = someone gives to you. もらう = to receive. The direction of giving determines which verb to use.

questions.question: 「田中さんは私に本をくれました」means:
options: I gave Mr. Tanaka a book
Mr. Tanaka gave me a book
I received a book from Mr. Tanaka
B and C are both correct
questions.answer: B and C are both correct
questions.explanation: くれる is used when someone gives something TO the speaker (or in-group). 田中さんは私にくれました = Mr. Tanaka gave (to me). This is equivalent to 私は田中さんにもらいました.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「今年」?
questions.explanation: 今年 (ことし / kotoshi) = this year. 来年 (らいねん) = next year, 去年 (きょねん) = last year.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「先週」?
questions.explanation: 先週 (せんしゅう / senshuu) = last week. 今週 (こんしゅう) = this week, 来週 (らいしゅう) = next week.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「午後」?
questions.explanation: 午後 (ごご / gogo) = PM / afternoon. 午前 (ごぜん / gozen) = AM / morning. 午 = noon.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「右手」?
questions.explanation: 右手 (みぎて / migite) = right hand. 右 (みぎ) = right, 手 (て) = hand.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「小学生」?
questions.explanation: 小学生 (しょうがくせい / shougakusei) = elementary school student. 小学校 (しょうがっこう) = elementary school.

questions.question: What does 「泳ぐ」(およぐ) mean?
questions.explanation: 泳ぐ (およぐ / oyogu) = to swim. It is a Group 1 (godan) verb ending in ぐ.

questions.question: What does 「話す」(はなす) mean?
questions.explanation: 話す (はなす / hanasu) = to speak, to talk. It is a Group 1 (godan) verb ending in す.

questions.question: What does 「使う」(つかう) mean?
questions.explanation: 使う (つかう / tsukau) = to use. It is a Group 1 (godan) verb ending in う.

questions.question: What does 「始まる」(はじまる) mean?
questions.explanation: 始まる (はじまる / hajimaru) = to begin/start (intransitive — the thing starts by itself). 始める (はじめる) = to begin something (transitive — you start it).

questions.question: What does 「終わる」(おわる) mean?
questions.explanation: 終わる (おわる / owaru) = to finish/end (intransitive). 終える (おえる) = to finish something (transitive).

questions.question: What is 「部屋」(へや)?
questions.explanation: 部屋 (へや / heya) = room (inside a building). 家 (いえ/うち) = house/home.

questions.question: What is 「窓」(まど)?
questions.explanation: 窓 (まど / mado) = window. ドア (doa) = door (from English), 天井 (てんじょう) = ceiling.

questions.question: What is 「地図」(ちず)?
questions.explanation: 地図 (ちず / chizu) = map. 地 = earth/land, 図 = diagram/map.

questions.question: What is 「財布」(さいふ)?
questions.explanation: 財布 (さいふ / saifu) = wallet or purse. 財 = wealth, 布 = cloth/fabric.

questions.question: What is 「鍵」(かぎ)?
questions.explanation: 鍵 (かぎ / kagi) = key. Also means lock (since a key and lock are conceptually linked in Japanese). かぎをかける = to lock.

questions.question: What does 「暇」(ひま) mean?
questions.explanation: 暇 (ひま / hima) = free (time), not busy. ひまです = I'm free / I have time. 忙しい (いそがしい) = busy.

questions.question: What does 「元気」(げんき) mean?
questions.explanation: 元気 (げんき / genki) = healthy, energetic, full of energy. お元気ですか = How are you? / Are you well?

questions.question: What does 「危ない」(あぶない) mean?
questions.explanation: 危ない (あぶない / abunai) = dangerous, unsafe. Often used as a warning: 危ない！= Watch out! / Danger!

questions.question: What is 「鳥」(とり)?
questions.explanation: 鳥 (とり / tori) = bird. Also means chicken/poultry when referring to food. 魚 (さかな) = fish.

questions.question: What is 「数学」(すうがく)?
questions.explanation: 数学 (すうがく / suugaku) = mathematics. 数 = number, 学 = study. 理科 (りか) = science, 歴史 (れきし) = history.

questions.question: 「田中さんも日本人です」– What does 「も」mean here?
questions.explanation: も (mo) = also, too. 田中さんも日本人です = Mr. Tanaka is also Japanese. も replaces は or が when adding 'also' to the sentence.

questions.question: 「りんごやバナナなど」– What does 「や～など」mean?
options: Exactly these items and nothing else
questions.explanation: や (ya) connects nouns in a non-exhaustive list (there are more items not listed). など = and so on/etc. Compare with と, which implies an exhaustive list.

questions.question: What is the て-form of 「急ぐ」(いそぐ, to hurry)?
questions.explanation: 急ぐ (isogu) ends in ぐ. The て-form rule for ぐ: → いで. 急ぐ → 急いで (isoide). Compare: く → いて (書く → 書いて), but ぐ → いで.

questions.question: What is the て-form of 「死ぬ」(しぬ, to die)?
questions.explanation: 死ぬ (shinu) ends in ぬ. The て-form rule: ぬ → んで. 死ぬ → 死んで (shinde). Same pattern as む: 飲む → 飲んで.

questions.question: What is the て-form of 「帰る」(かえる, to return home)?
questions.explanation: 帰る (kaeru) ends in る, but it is a Group 1 (godan) verb, not Group 2. The て-form for godan る verbs: る → って. 帰る → 帰って (kaette).

questions.question: 「学校の後で、図書館に行きました」means:
options: I went to school and the library
Before school, I went to the library
After school, I went to the library
Instead of school, I went to the library
questions.answer: After school, I went to the library
questions.explanation: 〜の後で (no ato de) = after ~. 学校の後で = after school. 〜の前に (no mae ni) = before ~.

questions.question: 「電車に乗る前に、切符を買います」means:
options: After buying a ticket, I ride the train
Before riding the train, I buy a ticket
I buy a ticket while riding the train
I buy a ticket instead of riding the train
questions.answer: Before riding the train, I buy a ticket
questions.explanation: 〜前に (mae ni) = before ~. 電車に乗る前に = before riding the train. The verb before 前に stays in dictionary form.

questions.question: 「ご飯を食べてから、歯を磨きます」means:
options: I brush my teeth before eating
After eating, I brush my teeth
While eating, I brush my teeth
I eat instead of brushing my teeth
questions.answer: After eating, I brush my teeth
questions.explanation: 〜てから (te kara) = after doing ~ / and then. 食べてから = after eating. It emphasizes sequence: first eat, then brush.

questions.question: Which of these is a na-adjective?
questions.explanation: きれい (kirei) = pretty/clean is a na-adjective despite ending in い. Na-adjectives: きれい, 好き, 嫌い, 静か, 有名, 元気, 大丈夫. Don't confuse with i-adjectives ending in い.

questions.question: How do na-adjectives modify nouns directly?
questions.explanation: Na-adjectives add な before nouns. 静かな部屋 = quiet room, 有名な人 = famous person. I-adjectives directly precede nouns: 大きい部屋 = big room.

questions.question: 「どんな音楽が好きですか」means:
options: What kind of music do you like?
How much music do you listen to?
questions.answer: What kind of music do you like?
questions.explanation: どんな (donna) = what kind of. Used before nouns to ask about the type/nature of something. どの = which (specific item), どう = how (manner).

questions.question: 「クラスの中で、だれが一番背が高いですか」means:
options: Who is the tallest in the class?
Who is taller than the class?
Who is very tall in the class?
questions.answer: Who is the tallest in the class?
questions.explanation: 一番 (いちばん / ichiban) = number one / the most. クラスの中で = in the class, 背が高い = tall, 一番 = most. Pattern: [scope]で、[noun]が一番～.

questions.question: 「一緒に映画を見ませんか」means:
options: Did you watch the movie together?
Why don't we watch a movie together? (invitation)
I don't want to watch movies with you
questions.answer: Why don't we watch a movie together? (invitation)
questions.explanation: ～ませんか (masen ka) is used for invitations and suggestions: 'Won't you ~?' / 'Would you like to ~?' 見ませんか = won't you watch? / shall we watch?

questions.question: What is the difference between 「～ましょう」and 「～ましょうか」?
options: ましょう = let's (proposal), ましょうか = shall I/we? (offer/check)
ましょう = question, ましょうか = statement
ましょう is formal, ましょうか is informal
questions.answer: ましょう = let's (proposal), ましょうか = shall I/we? (offer/check)
questions.explanation: 行きましょう = let's go (stronger proposal). 行きましょうか = shall we go? (checking/offering). ましょうか is softer and more consultative.

questions.question: 「先生に質問しました」– what role does 「に」play here?
options: Marks the indirect object (recipient/target of action)
questions.answer: Marks the indirect object (recipient/target of action)
questions.explanation: に (ni) marks the target/recipient of an action. 先生に質問する = ask the teacher (a question directed at the teacher). Similar: 友達に電話する = call a friend.

questions.question: How do you say 'two people' in Japanese?
questions.explanation: 人 (にん/り) is the counter for people. 1 person = 一人 (ひとり), 2 people = 二人 (ふたり). From 3 onwards: 三人 (さんにん), 四人 (よにん), etc.

questions.question: How do you say 'I am 20 years old'?
options: B and C are both correct
questions.answer: B and C are both correct
questions.explanation: 20 years old = 二十歳 (はたち / hatachi OR にじゅっさい). Both readings are acceptable. 歳/才 (さい) is the age counter.

questions.question: What is the negative te-form (ないで) used for?
options: Connecting actions where the first is NOT done, or making negative requests
questions.answer: Connecting actions where the first is NOT done, or making negative requests
questions.explanation: ないで (naide) = without doing ~ / not doing ~. 朝ごはんを食べないで学校へ行った = went to school without eating breakfast. Also: ～ないでください = please don't do ~.

questions.question: What does 「大丈夫」(だいじょうぶ) mean?
options: It's okay / No problem / I'm fine
questions.answer: It's okay / No problem / I'm fine
questions.explanation: 大丈夫 (だいじょうぶ / daijoubu) = okay, fine, alright, no problem. One of the most versatile expressions in Japanese.

questions.question: What does 「よろしくお願いします」mean?
options: Please treat me well / I'm in your care (multi-purpose polite expression)
questions.answer: Please treat me well / I'm in your care (multi-purpose polite expression)
questions.explanation: よろしくお願いします (yoroshiku onegaishimasu) is extremely versatile: used when meeting someone, making a request, asking for cooperation, or expressing anticipation of a good relationship.

questions.question: 「どうやって学校に来ましたか」means:
options: Why did you come to school?
When did you come to school?
How did you get to school?
Where did you go to school?
questions.answer: How did you get to school?
questions.explanation: どうやって (dou yatte) = how / by what means. It asks about the method or way of doing something.

questions.question: 「雨が降ったら、家にいます」means:
options: Because it rained, I am at home
If it rains, I will stay home
Even if it rains, I will go out
Although it is raining, I am at home
questions.answer: If it rains, I will stay home
questions.explanation: ～たら (tara) is a conditional form meaning 'if/when (something happens)'. 雨が降ったら = if it rains. It's one of four main conditional forms in Japanese.

questions.question: For the kanji 「三」, which is the correct stroke order?
options: Middle first, then top, then bottom
questions.explanation: 三 is written top to bottom: first the top horizontal stroke, then the middle, then the bottom. General kanji rule: top before bottom, left before right.

questions.question: What is the honorific/polite prefix added to many nouns in Japanese?
questions.explanation: お (o) and ご (go) are honorific prefixes. お is used with native Japanese words (お水, お金, お名前), ご with Sino-Japanese words (ご家族, ご住所). They add politeness and formality.

questions.question: 「お名前は何ですか」is a more polite way of saying which question?
questions.explanation: お名前は何ですか (onamae wa nan desu ka) = What is your name? (polite). The お prefix makes 名前 more honorific/respectful. 名前は何ですか is the plain version.

questions.question: What does 「待つ」(まつ) mean?
questions.explanation: 待つ (まつ / matsu) = to wait. Group 1 (godan) verb ending in つ. て-form: 待って (matte). ちょっと待って = wait a moment.

questions.question: What does 「貸す」(かす) mean?
questions.explanation: 貸す (かす / kasu) = to lend. The opposite is 借りる (かりる / kariru) = to borrow. 貸してください = please lend me (it).

questions.question: What does 「借りる」(かりる) mean?
questions.explanation: 借りる (かりる / kariru) = to borrow. Group 2 (ichidan) verb. Opposite: 貸す (かす) = to lend. 図書館で本を借りる = borrow a book from the library.

questions.question: What does 「洗う」(あらう) mean?
questions.explanation: 洗う (あらう / arau) = to wash. Group 1 verb ending in う. 手を洗う = wash hands, 皿を洗う = wash dishes.

questions.question: What does 「作る」(つくる) mean?
questions.explanation: 作る (つくる / tsukuru) = to make, to create, to cook. 料理を作る = make a meal. Group 1 (godan) verb ending in る.

questions.question: What does 「開ける」(あける) mean?
questions.explanation: 開ける (あける / akeru) = to open (transitive — you open something). Group 2 verb. Intransitive pair: 開く (あく) = to open (by itself). ドアを開ける = open the door.

questions.question: What does 「閉める」(しめる) mean?
questions.explanation: 閉める (しめる / shimeru) = to close (transitive). Group 2 verb. Intransitive pair: 閉まる (しまる) = to close (by itself). 窓を閉める = close the window.

questions.question: What does 「入れる」(いれる) mean?
questions.explanation: 入れる (いれる / ireru) = to put in, to insert. Group 2 verb. バッグに入れる = put into a bag. お茶を入れる = make tea (put/brew tea).

questions.question: What does 「出す」(だす) mean?
questions.explanation: 出す (だす / dasu) = to take out, submit, or send. 手紙を出す = send a letter. 宿題を出す = submit homework. Group 1 verb.

questions.question: What does 「遊ぶ」(あそぶ) mean?
questions.explanation: 遊ぶ (あそぶ / asobu) = to play, to hang out, to have fun. Used for both children playing and adults socializing. 友達と遊ぶ = hang out with friends.

questions.question: What does 「乗る」(のる) mean?
questions.explanation: 乗る (のる / noru) = to ride, to get on (a vehicle). 電車に乗る = ride the train. Opposite: 降りる (おりる) = to get off.

questions.question: What does 「降りる」(おりる) mean?
questions.explanation: 降りる (おりる / oriru) = to get off (a vehicle), to descend. Group 2 verb. 次の駅で降りる = get off at the next station. Opposite: 乗る = to get on.

questions.question: What does 「渡す」(わたす) mean?
questions.explanation: 渡す (わたす / watasu) = to hand over, to pass something to someone. 書類を渡す = hand over documents. Group 1 verb.

questions.question: What does 「渡る」(わたる) mean?
questions.explanation: 渡る (わたる / wataru) = to cross over (a road, bridge, river). 横断歩道を渡る = cross at the pedestrian crossing. Intransitive.

questions.question: What does 「走る」(はしる) mean?
questions.explanation: 走る (はしる / hashiru) = to run. Although it ends in る, it is a Group 1 (godan) verb. て-form: 走って.

questions.question: What does 「歩く」(あるく) mean?
questions.explanation: 歩く (あるく / aruku) = to walk. Group 1 verb ending in く. て-form: 歩いて (aruite). 歩いて行く = go on foot / walk there.

questions.question: What does 「曲がる」(まがる) mean?
questions.explanation: 曲がる (まがる / magaru) = to turn, to curve. 右に曲がる = turn right. Common in giving directions. Group 1 verb.

questions.question: What does 「止まる」(とまる) mean?
questions.explanation: 止まる (とまる / tomaru) = to stop (by itself, intransitive). 電車が止まる = the train stops. Transitive: 止める (とめる) = to stop something.

questions.question: What does 「忘れる」(わすれる) mean?
questions.explanation: 忘れる (わすれる / wasureru) = to forget. Group 2 verb. 名前を忘れる = forget a name. Opposite: 覚える (おぼえる) = to memorize/remember.

questions.question: What does 「覚える」(おぼえる) mean?
questions.explanation: 覚える (おぼえる / oboeru) = to memorize, to learn/remember. 単語を覚える = memorize vocabulary. Group 2 verb. Opposite: 忘れる = to forget.

questions.question: What does 「探す」(さがす) mean?
questions.explanation: 探す (さがす / sagasu) = to search for, to look for. 仕事を探す = look for a job. Group 1 verb. Note: 見つける (みつける) = to find.

questions.question: What does 「見せる」(みせる) mean?
questions.explanation: 見せる (みせる / miseru) = to show. Group 2 verb. 見せてください = please show me. パスポートを見せる = show a passport.

questions.question: What does 「教える」(おしえる) mean?
questions.explanation: 教える (おしえる / oshieru) = to teach, to tell, to inform. 日本語を教える = teach Japanese. 道を教える = give directions. Group 2 verb.

questions.question: What does 「習う」(ならう) mean?
questions.explanation: 習う (ならう / narau) = to learn (from a teacher/in a class). ピアノを習う = take piano lessons. Compare: 勉強する = to study, 学ぶ = to learn (broader).

questions.question: What does 「練習する」(れんしゅうする) mean?
questions.explanation: 練習する (れんしゅうする / renshuu suru) = to practice. It is a suru-verb (する verb). ピアノを練習する = practice piano.

questions.question: What does 「結婚する」(けっこんする) mean?
questions.explanation: 結婚する (けっこんする / kekkon suru) = to marry, to get married. Suru-verb. 結婚しています = is married (resultant state with ている).

questions.question: What does 「掃除する」(そうじする) mean?
questions.explanation: 掃除する (そうじする / souji suru) = to clean, to tidy up. Suru-verb. 部屋を掃除する = clean the room.

questions.question: What does 「料理する」(りょうりする) mean?
questions.explanation: 料理する (りょうりする / ryouri suru) = to cook. 料理 alone means 'cooking' or 'dish/cuisine'. Suru-verb.

questions.question: What does 「忙しい」(いそがしい) mean?
questions.explanation: 忙しい (いそがしい / isogashii) = busy. I-adjective. 今日はとても忙しい = I'm very busy today. Opposite: 暇 (ひま) = free/not busy.

questions.question: What does 「眠い」(ねむい) mean?
questions.explanation: 眠い (ねむい / nemui) = sleepy, drowsy. I-adjective. 眠いです = I'm sleepy. Related: 寝る (ねる) = to sleep.

questions.question: What does 「痛い」(いたい) mean?
questions.explanation: 痛い (いたい / itai) = painful, it hurts. 頭が痛い = I have a headache (head hurts). I-adjective.

questions.question: What does 「うるさい」mean?
questions.explanation: うるさい (urusai) = noisy, loud, annoying. I-adjective. うるさい！= Be quiet! / Shut up! (informal). Also used to mean 'fussy' about something.

questions.question: What does 「かわいい」mean?
questions.explanation: かわいい (kawaii) = cute, adorable. I-adjective. Widely used in Japanese culture and has been adopted internationally.

questions.question: What does 「かっこいい」mean?
questions.explanation: かっこいい (kakkoii) = cool, stylish, handsome. I-adjective (from 格好いい). Opposite: かっこ悪い (kakkо warui) = uncool.

questions.question: What does 「面白い」(おもしろい) mean?
questions.explanation: 面白い (おもしろい / omoshiroi) = interesting, funny, entertaining. I-adjective. Opposite: つまらない = boring.

questions.question: What does 「怖い」(こわい) mean?
questions.explanation: 怖い (こわい / kowai) = scary, frightening. I-adjective. 怖い映画 = scary movie. 怖い！= Scary! / I'm scared!

questions.question: What does 「やさしい」mean?
questions.explanation: やさしい has two kanji: 優しい (やさしい) = kind/gentle, and 易しい (やさしい) = easy. Context determines meaning. Both are N5 level words.

questions.question: What does 「辛い」(からい) mean?
questions.explanation: 辛い (からい / karai) = spicy, hot (taste). I-adjective. Note: 辛い can also be read つらい (tsurai) meaning 'painful/hard (emotionally)'.

questions.question: What does 「甘い」(あまい) mean?
questions.explanation: 甘い (あまい / amai) = sweet. I-adjective. Taste words: 甘い(sweet), 辛い(spicy), 酸っぱい(sour), 苦い(bitter), 塩辛い(salty).

questions.question: What is 「午前」(ごぜん)?
questions.explanation: 午前 (ごぜん / gozen) = AM, morning (before noon). 午後 (ごご) = PM, afternoon. 午 = noon.

questions.question: What is 「晩ご飯」(ばんごはん)?
questions.explanation: 晩ご飯 (ばんごはん / ban gohan) = dinner, evening meal. 朝ご飯 (あさごはん) = breakfast, 昼ご飯 (ひるごはん) = lunch.

questions.question: What is 「お茶」(おちゃ)?
questions.explanation: お茶 (おちゃ / ocha) = tea (usually green tea in Japanese context). The お is an honorific prefix. 紅茶 (こうちゃ) = black/red tea.

questions.question: What is 「牛乳」(ぎゅうにゅう)?
questions.explanation: 牛乳 (ぎゅうにゅう / gyuunyuu) = milk. 牛 = cow, 乳 = milk/breast. Also commonly called ミルク (miruku) from English.

questions.question: What is 「肉」(にく)?
questions.explanation: 肉 (にく / niku) = meat. 牛肉 (ぎゅうにく) = beef, 豚肉 (ぶたにく) = pork, 鶏肉 (とりにく) = chicken.

questions.question: What is 「野菜」(やさい)?
questions.explanation: 野菜 (やさい / yasai) = vegetable(s). 果物 (くだもの) = fruit.

questions.question: What is 「魚」(さかな)?
questions.explanation: 魚 (さかな / sakana) = fish. Also read うお (uo) in compounds. 魚屋 (さかなや) = fish shop/monger.

questions.question: What is 「卵」(たまご)?
questions.explanation: 卵 (たまご / tamago) = egg. 卵焼き (たまごやき) = Japanese rolled omelette. Also written as 玉子 in some contexts (especially in sushi).

questions.question: What is 「パン」?
questions.explanation: パン (pan) = bread. Loanword from Portuguese 'pão'. パン屋 (パンや) = bakery.

questions.question: What is 「果物」(くだもの)?
questions.explanation: 果物 (くだもの / kudamono) = fruit. 果 = fruit/result, 物 = thing. りんご = apple, バナナ = banana, みかん = mandarin orange.

questions.question: What is 「砂糖」(さとう)?
questions.explanation: 砂糖 (さとう / satou) = sugar. 砂 = sand, 糖 = sugar/sweet. 塩 (しお) = salt.

questions.question: What is 「椅子」(いす)?
questions.explanation: 椅子 (いす / isu) = chair. 机 (つくえ) = desk, テーブル = table.

questions.question: What is 「冷蔵庫」(れいぞうこ)?
questions.explanation: 冷蔵庫 (れいぞうこ / reizouko) = refrigerator. 冷 = cold, 蔵 = storage, 庫 = storehouse.

questions.question: What is 「自転車」(じてんしゃ)?
questions.explanation: 自転車 (じてんしゃ / jitensha) = bicycle. 自 = self, 転 = roll/rotate, 車 = vehicle. 自転車で行く = go by bicycle.

questions.question: What is 「地下鉄」(ちかてつ)?
questions.explanation: 地下鉄 (ちかてつ / chikatetsu) = subway, underground railway. 地下 = underground, 鉄 = iron/steel (train).

questions.question: What is 「新幹線」(しんかんせん)?
questions.explanation: 新幹線 (しんかんせん / shinkansen) = bullet train / Shinkansen. 新 = new, 幹 = trunk/main, 線 = line. Japan's high-speed rail network.

questions.question: What is 「手」(て)?
questions.explanation: 手 (て / te) = hand. Also used in compounds: 右手 (みぎて) = right hand, 左手 (ひだりて) = left hand.

questions.question: What is 「足」(あし)?
questions.explanation: 足 (あし / ashi) = foot or leg (Japanese does not always distinguish between the two). 手 (て) = hand/arm.

questions.question: What is 「頭」(あたま)?
questions.explanation: 頭 (あたま / atama) = head. 頭が痛い (あたまがいたい) = I have a headache.

questions.question: What is 「お腹」(おなか)?
questions.explanation: お腹 (おなか / onaka) = stomach, belly. お腹が痛い = stomachache. お腹が空いた (すいた) = I'm hungry.

questions.question: What is 「歯」(は)?
questions.explanation: 歯 (は / ha) = tooth/teeth. 歯を磨く = brush teeth. 歯医者 (はいしゃ) = dentist.

questions.question: What is 「靴」(くつ)?
questions.explanation: 靴 (くつ / kutsu) = shoes. 靴下 (くつした) = socks (literally 'under shoes'). 靴を履く (はく) = to put on shoes.

questions.question: What is 「帽子」(ぼうし)?
questions.explanation: 帽子 (ぼうし / boushi) = hat, cap. 帽子をかぶる = to wear a hat (note: かぶる = put on for items worn on the head).

questions.question: Which verb is used for putting on clothes (shirt, pants, dress)?
questions.explanation: 着る (きる / kiru) = to put on / wear (upper body or full body clothing: shirts, jackets, dresses). はく = shoes/pants/socks, かぶる = hats, する = accessories.

questions.question: What is 「海」(うみ)?
questions.explanation: 海 (うみ / umi) = sea, ocean. 山 (やま) = mountain, 川 (かわ) = river, 湖 (みずうみ) = lake.

questions.question: What is 「花」(はな)?
questions.explanation: 花 (はな / hana) = flower. Note: 鼻 (はな) = nose — same pronunciation but different kanji! 花見 (はなみ) = flower viewing (cherry blossoms).

questions.question: What is 「空」(そら)?
questions.explanation: 空 (そら / sora) = sky. Also read くう/から meaning 'empty'. 空が青い = the sky is blue.

questions.question: What is 「教室」(きょうしつ)?
questions.explanation: 教室 (きょうしつ / kyoushitsu) = classroom. 教 = teach, 室 = room.

questions.question: What is 「黒板」(こくばん)?
questions.explanation: 黒板 (こくばん / kokuban) = blackboard. 黒 = black, 板 = board. Nowadays often refers to any classroom board.

questions.question: What is 「会社員」(かいしゃいん)?
questions.explanation: 会社員 (かいしゃいん / kaishain) = company employee, office worker. 会社 = company, 員 = member/staff.

questions.question: What is 「医者」(いしゃ)?
questions.explanation: 医者 (いしゃ / isha) = doctor. Also: お医者さん (おいしゃさん) with honorific. 病院の医者 = hospital doctor.

questions.question: What is 「音楽」(おんがく)?
questions.explanation: 音楽 (おんがく / ongaku) = music. 音 = sound, 楽 = enjoyment/music. 音楽を聴く = listen to music.

questions.question: What is 「旅行」(りょこう)?
questions.explanation: 旅行 (りょこう / ryokou) = travel, trip. 旅行する = to travel. 海外旅行 = overseas travel.

questions.question: What is 「写真」(しゃしん)?
questions.explanation: 写真 (しゃしん / shashin) = photograph, photo. 写真を撮る (とる) = take a photo. 写真家 = photographer.

questions.question: What is 「公園」(こうえん)?
questions.explanation: 公園 (こうえん / kouen) = park. 公 = public, 園 = garden/park. 公園で遊ぶ = play at the park.

questions.question: What is 「図書館」(としょかん)?
questions.explanation: 図書館 (としょかん / toshokan) = library. 図書 = books/documents, 館 = building/hall. 本屋 (ほんや) = bookstore.

questions.question: What is 「銀行」(ぎんこう)?
questions.explanation: 銀行 (ぎんこう / ginkou) = bank. 銀 = silver, 行 = go/institution. 銀行口座 = bank account.

questions.question: What is 「薬局」(やっきょく)?
questions.explanation: 薬局 (やっきょく / yakkyoku) = pharmacy, drugstore. 薬 (くすり) = medicine/drug, 局 = office/bureau.

questions.question: What is 「洗濯」(せんたく)?
questions.explanation: 洗濯 (せんたく / sentaku) = laundry, washing clothes. 洗濯する = do laundry. 洗濯機 (せんたくき) = washing machine.

questions.question: What is 「ゴミ」?
questions.explanation: ゴミ (gomi) = trash, garbage, rubbish. ゴミを出す = take out the trash. ゴミ箱 (ごみばこ) = trash can.

questions.question: What is 「値段」(ねだん)?
questions.explanation: 値段 (ねだん / nedan) = price. 値段はいくらですか = How much is the price? Also: 料金 (りょうきん) = fee/charge, 代金 (だいきん) = cost.

questions.question: What is 「レシート」?
questions.explanation: レシート (reshiito) = receipt. From English 'receipt'. Also: 領収書 (りょうしゅうしょ) is the more formal word for receipt.

questions.question: What is 「メール」?
questions.explanation: メール (meeru) = email or text message (from English 'mail'). メールを送る = send an email. 手紙 (てがみ) = traditional letter.

questions.question: What is 「番号」(ばんごう)?
questions.explanation: 番号 (ばんごう / bangou) = number (as an identifier, not a quantity). 電話番号 = phone number, 番号札 = number ticket.

questions.question: What is 「来月」(らいげつ)?
questions.explanation: 来月 (らいげつ / raigetsu) = next month. 先月 (せんげつ) = last month, 今月 (こんげつ) = this month.

questions.question: What is 「朝」(あさ)?
questions.explanation: 朝 (あさ / asa) = morning. 昼 (ひる) = noon/daytime, 夕方 (ゆうがた) = evening, 夜 (よる) = night.

questions.question: What is 「夜」(よる)?
questions.explanation: 夜 (よる / yoru) = night. 今夜 (こんや) = tonight. 夜ご飯 = dinner (literally 'night meal', informal variant of 晩ご飯).

questions.question: 「〜時間」(じかん) vs 「〜時」(じ) — what is the difference?
options: 時間 = duration (X hours), 時 = specific time (X o'clock)
questions.answer: 時間 = duration (X hours), 時 = specific time (X o'clock)
questions.explanation: 三時 (さんじ) = 3 o'clock (point in time). 三時間 (さんじかん) = 3 hours (duration). This distinction is crucial in Japanese.

questions.question: How do you say '10,000' in Japanese?
questions.explanation: 万 (まん / man) = 10,000. Japanese counts in units of 万, unlike English which uses thousands. 一万 = 10,000, 十万 = 100,000, 百万 = 1,000,000.

questions.question: How do you say '500' in Japanese?
questions.explanation: 五百 (ごひゃく / go-hyaku) = 500. Note the sound change: 百 (ひゃく), but 三百 (さんびゃく), 六百 (ろっぴゃく), 八百 (はっぴゃく).

questions.question: Which counter is used for books and magazines?
questions.explanation: 冊 (さつ) counts bound books and magazines. 一冊 (いっさつ), 二冊 (にさつ), 三冊 (さんさつ). 本 = long thin objects, 枚 = flat thin things.

questions.question: Which counter is used for floors of a building?
questions.explanation: 階 (かい) = floor/story of a building. 一階 (いっかい) = 1st floor, 二階 (にかい) = 2nd floor. Note: 一階 can also be read いちかい.

questions.question: Which counter is used for glasses/cups of liquid?
questions.explanation: 杯 (はい) counts cups, glasses, bowls of liquid. 一杯 (いっぱい) = one cup/glass. 一杯 also means 'full' as a separate usage.

questions.question: Which counter is used for thin flat objects like paper and plates?
questions.explanation: 枚 (まい) = flat, thin objects. 紙一枚 = one sheet of paper, 皿三枚 = three plates. 一枚 (いちまい), 二枚 (にまい).

questions.question: How do you count nights of a stay (e.g. at a hotel)?
questions.explanation: 泊 (はく) counts nights of lodging. 一泊 (いっぱく) = one night, 二泊 (にはく) = two nights. 一泊二日 = one night, two days (common travel expression).

questions.question: Which counter is used for times/occurrences (e.g. 'three times')?
questions.explanation: Both 回 (かい) and 度 (ど) count occurrences/times. 一回 = once, 二回 = twice. 一度 = once, 二度 = twice. They are often interchangeable at N5 level.

questions.question: Which kanji means 'rain'?
questions.explanation: 雨 (あめ / ame) = rain. 雪 (ゆき) = snow, 風 (かぜ) = wind, 雲 (くも) = cloud.

questions.question: Which kanji means 'gold' or 'money' or 'Friday'?
questions.explanation: 金 (きん/かね) = gold, money. Also: 金曜日 (きんようび) = Friday. 銀 = silver, 鉄 = iron, 銅 = copper.

questions.question: Which kanji means 'earth' or 'soil' or 'Saturday'?
questions.explanation: 土 (つち/ど) = earth, soil, ground. Also: 土曜日 (どようび) = Saturday. The 7 days use the 5 elements: 月火水木金土日.

questions.question: Which kanji means 'old' (as in age/time)?
questions.explanation: 古 (ふるい / furui as adjective, こ / ko in compounds) = old (of things, not people). 古い車 = old car. 新しい (あたらしい) = new.

questions.question: Which kanji means 'long'?
questions.explanation: 長 (なが/ちょう) = long. 長い (ながい) = long (i-adjective). Also means 'chief/head': 社長 (しゃちょう) = company president.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「来週」?
questions.explanation: 来週 (らいしゅう / raishuu) = next week. 来 = come/next. 今週 = this week, 先週 = last week.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「東西南北」?
options: ひがしにしみなみきた
Both A and C are partially correct
questions.explanation: 東西南北 (とうざいなんぼく / touzainanboku) = east, west, south, north (the four cardinal directions as a set phrase). Individual readings: 東(ひがし)西(にし)南(みなみ)北(きた).

questions.question: What is the reading of 「食堂」?
questions.explanation: 食堂 (しょくどう / shokudou) = cafeteria, dining hall, diner. 食 = eat/food, 堂 = hall.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「手紙」?
questions.explanation: 手紙 (てがみ / tegami) = letter (the written communication). 手 = hand, 紙 = paper. Note the voiced reading: かみ → がみ.

questions.question: What is the reading of 「外出」?
questions.explanation: 外出 (がいしゅつ / gaishutsu) = going out, being away from home. 外 = outside, 出 = go out. 外出する = to go out.

questions.question: What does 「入学」(にゅうがく) mean?
questions.explanation: 入学 (にゅうがく / nyuugaku) = school enrollment, matriculation. 入 = enter, 学 = study/school. 入学式 = entrance ceremony. Opposite: 卒業 (そつぎょう) = graduation.

questions.question: What does 「名前」(なまえ) mean?
questions.explanation: 名前 (なまえ / namae) = name. 名 = name/famous, 前 = front/before. お名前は? = What is your name? (polite)

questions.question: What does 「来年」(らいねん) mean?
questions.explanation: 来年 (らいねん / rainen) = next year. 来 = come (implies arrival/future). 去年 (きょねん) = last year, 今年 (ことし) = this year.

questions.question: What does 「国語」(こくご) mean?
questions.explanation: 国語 (こくご / kokugo) = national language; in Japan this means Japanese as a school subject. 国 = country, 語 = language.

questions.question: What does 「下車」(げしゃ) mean?
questions.explanation: 下車 (げしゃ / gesha) = getting off a vehicle (formal/written). 下 = down/get off, 車 = vehicle. Used on train announcements.

questions.question: 「友達と映画を見ました」– what does 「と」mean here?
questions.explanation: と (to) with a person means 'together with'. 友達と = with a friend. Compare: りんごとバナナ = apples and bananas (listing nouns).

questions.question: 「電話で話しました」– what does 「で」mean here?
questions.explanation: で (de) marks the means or tool used for an action. 電話で = by phone / via telephone. Also: 日本語で話す = speak in Japanese, バスで行く = go by bus.

questions.question: 「一人で行きます」– what nuance does 「で」add here?
questions.explanation: 一人で (ひとりで) = alone, by oneself. で here marks the manner/condition. 一人で = as one person = alone.

questions.question: 「この電車は渋谷に止まりますか」– Which particle marks destination here?
questions.explanation: に (ni) marks the location where the train stops. に also marks the destination of movement, the time of an action, and the target of an action.

questions.question: What is the function of 「ね」at the end of a sentence?
options: Seeks agreement or confirmation from the listener
questions.answer: Seeks agreement or confirmation from the listener
questions.explanation: ね (ne) is a sentence-final particle seeking confirmation or sharing feelings: 'isn't it?' / 'right?'. 今日は暑いですね = It's hot today, isn't it? Compare with よ (yo) = assertion.

questions.question: What is the function of 「よ」at the end of a sentence?
options: Asserts new information to the listener
questions.answer: Asserts new information to the listener
questions.explanation: よ (yo) asserts information the speaker believes the listener doesn't know: 'I'm telling you' / 'you know'. もう三時ですよ = It's already 3 o'clock (you should know). Opposite tone from ね.

questions.question: What does the 〜ている form express for state-change verbs like 「結婚する」?
options: Currently in the process of marrying
The resultant state of having married (is married)
questions.answer: The resultant state of having married (is married)
questions.explanation: For verbs describing a change of state (結婚する, 死ぬ, 着る), 〜ている expresses the resultant state: 結婚しています = is married. 着ています = is wearing (the garment is on).

questions.question: What does 「〜に行く」mean?
options: To come for the purpose of ~
To go for the purpose of ~
questions.answer: To go for the purpose of ~
questions.explanation: 〜に行く (ni iku) = to go (somewhere) for the purpose of doing ~. The purpose verb takes the stem (ます-form without ます) + に. 買い物に行く = go shopping.

questions.question: What does 「〜に来る」mean?
options: To go for the purpose of ~
To come for the purpose of ~
questions.answer: To come for the purpose of ~
questions.explanation: 〜に来る (ni kuru) = to come for the purpose of doing ~. 遊びに来る = come to hang out/visit. Same structure as 〜に行く but with来る.

questions.question: What does 「〜てみる」mean?
questions.explanation: 〜てみる (te miru) = to try doing something (to see what it's like). 食べてみる = try eating. みる (see/watch) adds the nuance of 'trying to see/experience'.

questions.question: What does 「〜てしまう」express?
options: To do something completely / accidentally / regrettably
questions.answer: To do something completely / accidentally / regrettably
questions.explanation: 〜てしまう (te shimau) expresses: (1) completion of an action, (2) accidental action, (3) regrettable action. 財布を忘れてしまった = I (unfortunately) forgot my wallet.

questions.question: What does 「〜ておく」mean?
options: To do something and leave it as is (for future use/preparation)
To do something in advance regrettably
questions.answer: To do something and leave it as is (for future use/preparation)
questions.explanation: 〜ておく (te oku) = to do something in advance and leave it as is. 予約しておく = make a reservation in advance (and leave it set). Expresses preparation.

questions.question: 「寒ければ、コートを着てください」– what form is 〜れば?
questions.explanation: 〜れば (reba) is one of four conditional forms. For i-adjectives: remove い, add ければ. 寒ければ = if it is cold. For verbs, replace the final う-sound with えば.

questions.question: What is the difference between 〜と and 〜たら as conditionals?
options: と = natural/inevitable result, たら = general if-then (including hypotheticals and single events)
たら = natural result, と = hypothetical
Both only used for future events
questions.answer: と = natural/inevitable result, たら = general if-then (including hypotheticals and single events)
questions.explanation: 〜と expresses natural/automatic consequences (春になると、桜が咲く = when spring comes, cherry blossoms bloom). 〜たら is more general and can be used for hypotheticals, one-time events, and discovery.

questions.question: What is the て-form of the i-adjective 「寒い」(cold)?
questions.explanation: I-adjective て-form: replace い with くて. 寒い → 寒くて. Used to connect adjective descriptions: 今日は寒くて、雨です = Today it's cold and rainy.

questions.question: What is the て-form of the na-adjective 「便利」(convenient)?
questions.explanation: Na-adjective て-form: add で. 便利で = being convenient (and...). 駅に近くて便利です = It's close to the station and convenient.

questions.question: In「昨日食べたケーキはおいしかった」, what modifies ケーキ?
options: 昨日食べた (the cake that I ate yesterday)
questions.answer: 昨日食べた (the cake that I ate yesterday)
questions.explanation: In Japanese, relative clauses come BEFORE the noun they modify, in plain form. 昨日食べた = [that I ate yesterday] modifies ケーキ (cake). Japanese relative clauses do not use relative pronouns like 'that/which'.

questions.question: What does 「〜かもしれません」express?
questions.explanation: 〜かもしれません (kamoshiremasen) = might be, maybe, possibly. 雨が降るかもしれません = It might rain. Less certain than でしょう.

questions.question: What does 「〜と思います」express?
questions.explanation: 〜と思います (to omoimasu) = I think (that) ~. 明日は晴れると思います = I think it will be sunny tomorrow. Uses the plain form + と思います.

questions.question: How do you say 'Let's meet at 2:30'?
options: 二時半に会いましょう
二時三十分に会いましょう
二半時に会いましょう
questions.explanation: 二時半 (にじはん) = 2:30, using 半 (half past). 二時三十分 (にじさんじゅっぷん) = 2:30, using minutes. Both are correct and commonly used.

questions.question: 「どちら」vs 「どこ」– what is the difference?
options: どちら = which of two choices / polite 'where', どこ = where (general)
どこ = which, どちら = where
どちら is informal, どこ is formal
questions.answer: どちら = which of two choices / polite 'where', どこ = where (general)
questions.explanation: どこ = where (general). どちら = which direction / which of two / polite form of where. お手洗いはどちらですか = Where is the restroom? (polite). どちらが好きですか = Which do you like?

questions.question: 「いつ」means what?
questions.explanation: いつ (itsu) = when. 誕生日はいつですか = When is your birthday? Unlike English, Japanese question words don't always move to the front of the sentence.

questions.question: 「なぜ」/ 「どうして」mean what?
questions.explanation: なぜ (naze) and どうして (doushite) both mean 'why'. どうして is more conversational. なぜ is slightly more formal/literary. なんで (nande) is the most casual form.

questions.question: Which demonstrative is used for things near the listener?
questions.explanation: Japanese uses a 3-way system: こ (near speaker), そ (near listener), あ (far from both). その本 = that book [near you]. この本 = this book [near me]. あの本 = that book [over there].

questions.question: What is the difference between 「この」and 「これ」?
options: この is used alone, これ must precede a noun
この precedes a noun, これ stands alone as a pronoun
この is polite, これ is casual
questions.answer: この precedes a noun, これ stands alone as a pronoun
questions.explanation: この (kono) = this [noun] — must be followed by a noun: この本 = this book. これ (kore) = this one — stands alone: これはなんですか = What is this?

questions.question: 「〜はどうですか」means:
options: How about ~ ? / What do you think of ~ ?
questions.answer: How about ~ ? / What do you think of ~ ?
questions.explanation: 〜はどうですか (wa dou desu ka) = How about ~? / What do you think of ~? Used for suggestions or asking opinions. コーヒーはどうですか = How about (some) coffee?

questions.question: 「〜ましょうか」used when offering to do something means:
questions.explanation: 〜ましょうか can mean 'shall I?' when offering help. 荷物を持ちましょうか = Shall I carry your luggage? Compare with 〜ましょう (let's ~) and 〜ましょうか (shall we? / shall I?).

questions.question: 「〜でも〜ますか」(e.g. お茶でも飲みますか) – what does でも mean here?
options: Even tea / tea or something (softens the suggestion)
questions.answer: Even tea / tea or something (softens the suggestion)
questions.explanation: でも in this context = 'or something like that', softening a suggestion. お茶でも飲みますか = Would you like some tea or something? Less direct than お茶を飲みますか.

questions.question: 「〜なくてもいいです」means:
questions.explanation: 〜なくてもいいです (nakute mo ii desu) = don't have to / need not. 宿題をしなくてもいいです = You don't have to do homework. Opposite: 〜なければなりません = must do.

questions.question: 「〜そうです」(e.g. おいしそうです) means:
questions.explanation: 〜そうです (sou desu) after an adjective stem = looks/seems based on visual evidence. おいしそう = looks delicious. Attach to i-adj stem (remove い), or na-adj directly.

questions.question: 「〜そうです」after a plain form sentence (e.g. 雨が降るそうです) means:
options: It looks like it will rain (based on appearance)
questions.explanation: Plain form + そうです = hearsay / reported speech ('I heard that...'). 雨が降るそうです = I heard it will rain. Different from adjective stem + そう (looks like...).

questions.question: 「いただく」is the humble form of which verb?
questions.explanation: いただく (itadaku) is the humble/respectful form of もらう (to receive). Used when receiving from someone of higher status: 先生にいただきました = I received it from my teacher.

questions.question: 「申します」(もうします) is the humble form of which verb?
questions.explanation: 申す (もうす) / 申します is the humble form of 言う (to say). Used when referring to your own name or speech: 田中と申します = My name is Tanaka (formal self-introduction).

questions.question: 「りんごを三つください」– which type of counting is used?
options: Native Japanese counting (ひとつ, ふたつ, みっつ)
questions.answer: Native Japanese counting (ひとつ, ふたつ, みっつ)
questions.explanation: 三つ (みっつ) is native Japanese counting (和語数詞). Used for general objects 1-10 without a specific counter. 一つ(ひとつ)二つ(ふたつ)三つ(みっつ)四つ(よっつ)五つ(いつつ)...

questions.question: 「三時間」means:
questions.explanation: 三時間 (さんじかん) = 3 hours of duration. 三時 (さんじ) = 3 o'clock. Adding 間 (かん) to 時 (じ) creates a duration expression.

questions.passage: スミスさんはアメリカ人です。今、日本の会社で働いています。日本語がとても上手です。毎日電車で会社に行きます。
questions.question: What nationality is Mr. Smith?
questions.explanation: スミスさんはアメリカ人です = Mr. Smith is American. アメリカ人 = American person.

questions.passage: スミスさんはアメリカ人です。今、日本の会社で働いています。日本語がとても上手です。毎日電車で会社に行きます。
questions.question: How does Mr. Smith get to work?
questions.explanation: 毎日電車で会社に行きます = goes to the company by train every day. 電車で = by train.

questions.passage: 私のへやに机が一つと、いすが二つあります。本棚には本がたくさんあります。まどのそばにねこが一匹います。
questions.question: How many chairs are in the room?
questions.explanation: いすが二つあります = there are two chairs. 二つ (ふたつ) = two (native Japanese counting).

questions.passage: 私のへやに机が一つと、いすが二つあります。本棚には本がたくさんあります。まどのそばにねこが一匹います。
questions.question: Where is the cat?
questions.explanation: まどのそばにねこが一匹います = there is one cat by the window. そば = near/beside.

questions.passage: 今日は父の誕生日です。夕方、家族でレストランに行きます。父はすしが好きですから、すし屋に行くつもりです。
questions.question: Whose birthday is it?
questions.explanation: 今日は父の誕生日です = Today is my father's birthday. 父 (ちち) = my (own) father.

questions.passage: 今日は父の誕生日です。夕方、家族でレストランに行きます。父はすしが好きですから、すし屋に行くつもりです。
questions.question: What type of restaurant will they go to?
questions.explanation: すし屋に行くつもりです = plan to go to a sushi restaurant. 父はすしが好きですから = because father likes sushi.

questions.passage: 日本語教室 毎週火曜日・木曜日 午後6時〜8時 場所：市民センター 料金：月3,000円
questions.question: On which days does the Japanese class meet?
questions.explanation: 火曜日 (かようび) = Tuesday, 木曜日 (もくようび) = Thursday. 毎週 = every week.

questions.passage: 日本語教室 毎週火曜日・木曜日 午後6時〜8時 場所：市民センター 料金：月3,000円
questions.question: What is the monthly fee?
questions.explanation: 料金：月3,000円 = fee: 3,000 yen per month. 料金 (りょうきん) = fee/charge, 月 (つき/げつ) = month.

questions.passage: 山田さんは毎朝ジョギングをします。雨の日でも走ります。健康のためにしています。
questions.question: What does Mr. Yamada do every morning?
questions.explanation: 毎朝ジョギングをします = does jogging every morning. ジョギング = jogging.

questions.passage: 山田さんは毎朝ジョギングをします。雨の日でも走ります。健康のためにしています。
questions.question: Why does Mr. Yamada do this?
options: Because a doctor told him to
questions.explanation: 健康のためにしています = does it for the sake of health. 健康 (けんこう) = health, ため = for the sake of.

questions.passage: ランチメニュー：ラーメン 800円、カレーライス 700円、うどん 600円、サンドイッチ 500円
questions.question: Which is the most expensive item on the lunch menu?
questions.explanation: ラーメン = 800円 is the highest price. カレーライス = 700, うどん = 600, サンドイッチ = 500.

questions.passage: ランチメニュー：ラーメン 800円、カレーライス 700円、うどん 600円、サンドイッチ 500円
questions.question: If you order ramen and a sandwich, how much will you pay?
questions.explanation: ラーメン 800円 + サンドイッチ 500円 = 1,300円.

questions.question: A friend says 「お疲れ様」(おつかれさま). What is the appropriate response?
options: お疲れ様です / お疲れ
questions.answer: お疲れ様です / お疲れ
questions.explanation: お疲れ様 (otsukaresamа) = thank you for your hard work / good job. The standard response is also お疲れ様です. Used among colleagues at end of work or effort.

questions.question: You return home and say「ただいま」. What does your family reply?
questions.explanation: ただいま (tadaima) = I'm home! おかえり(なさい) (okaeri/nasai) = Welcome back! These are set home-arrival phrases. いってらっしゃい = said when someone leaves the house.

questions.question: When someone leaves the house for work/school, what do they say?
questions.explanation: いってきます (ittekimasu) = I'm going and coming back / I'll be off. The family responds: いってらっしゃい (itterasshai) = Have a good trip / Go and come back safely.

questions.question: Before going to sleep, you say:
questions.explanation: おやすみなさい (oyasuminasai) = Good night. The casual form is おやすみ. Said before sleeping or parting at night.

questions.question: What does 「ごちそうさまでした」express?
options: Said when giving food to someone
Said after finishing a meal (thank you for the feast)
questions.answer: Said after finishing a meal (thank you for the feast)
questions.explanation: ごちそうさまでした (gochisousamadeshita) = said after a meal to express gratitude. Paired with いただきます (before eating). ごちそう = feast/treat.

questions.question: You want to ask a stranger for directions. How do you start the conversation?
options: すみません、ちょっといいですか
よろしくおねがいします
questions.answer: すみません、ちょっといいですか
questions.explanation: すみません、ちょっといいですか = Excuse me, do you have a moment? This is the natural way to approach a stranger. すみません alone also works as an opener.

questions.question: 「お先にどうぞ」means:
questions.explanation: お先にどうぞ (osakini douzo) = Please go ahead / After you. お先に = before you, どうぞ = please (go ahead). A polite gesture to let someone pass or go first.

questions.question: 「どうぞよろしく」is often said when:
options: Meeting someone for the first time
questions.answer: Meeting someone for the first time
questions.explanation: どうぞよろしく (douzo yoroshiku) = Please treat me well / Nice to meet you. Often said after はじめまして (hajimemashite) in first introductions.

questions.question: What hiragana represents the sound 'tsu'?
questions.explanation: つ = tsu. The ta-row: た(ta) ち(chi) つ(tsu) て(te) と(to). Note that ち = chi and つ = tsu, not 'ti' and 'tu'.

questions.question: What is the small っ (small tsu) used for?
options: To represent the sound 'tsu' more softly
To indicate a double consonant (geminate) — a brief pause before the next consonant
To change a vowel to a nasal sound
questions.answer: To indicate a double consonant (geminate) — a brief pause before the next consonant
questions.explanation: Small っ (促音/sokuon) indicates a doubled consonant: きって (kitte) = stamp, ざっし (zasshi) = magazine. It takes one mora (beat) of silence/pause.

questions.question: What are the dakuten (voiced) versions of か, さ, た, は rows called?
options: が, ざ, だ, ば
が, ざ, た, ぱ
か, さ, だ, は
か, さ, た, ぱ
questions.answer: が, ざ, だ, ば
questions.explanation: Dakuten (゛) voicing: か→が, さ→ざ, た→だ, は→ば. The は-row voiced is ば (ba). The は-row also has a half-voiced (handakuten ゜) form: ぱ (pa).

questions.question: What word does 「スマートフォン」represent?
questions.explanation: スマートフォン (sumaatofon) = smartphone. From English 'smartphone'. Often shortened to スマホ (sumaho) in everyday speech.

questions.question: What word does 「アパート」represent?
questions.explanation: アパート (apaato) = apartment. From English 'apartment'. In Japan, アパート usually refers to a smaller wooden/light-steel building, while マンション = larger concrete building.

questions.question: What word does 「ノート」represent?
questions.explanation: ノート (nooto) = notebook. From English 'note'. In Japan, ノート typically means a lined writing notebook. 手帳 (てちょう) = personal organizer/planner.

questions.question: What word does 「エアコン」represent?
questions.explanation: エアコン (eakon) = air conditioner. Shortened from エアーコンディショナー (air conditioner). Very common loanword shortening in Japanese.

questions.question: What word does 「バイト」represent?
questions.explanation: バイト (baito) = part-time job. From German 'Arbeit' (work), not English. アルバイト (arubaito) is the full form. Very common in Japanese.

questions.question: What word does 「チケット」represent?
questions.explanation: チケット (chiketto) = ticket. From English 'ticket'. 切符 (きっぷ) is the traditional Japanese word for train ticket.

questions.question: What word does 「プール」represent?
questions.explanation: プール (puuru) = swimming pool. From English 'pool'. 水泳 (すいえい) = swimming (the sport).

questions.question: What does 「おめでとうございます」mean?
questions.explanation: おめでとうございます (omedetou gozaimasu) = Congratulations! (formal). おめでとう = casual form. 誕生日おめでとう = Happy Birthday!

questions.question: What does 「お久しぶりです」(おひさしぶりです) mean?
questions.explanation: お久しぶりです (ohisashiburi desu) = long time no see. Used when meeting someone you haven't seen for a while. 久しぶり (hisashiburi) is the casual form.

questions.question: What does 「お邪魔します」(おじゃまします) mean?
options: Excuse me for intruding (said when entering someone's home/room)
questions.answer: Excuse me for intruding (said when entering someone's home/room)
questions.explanation: お邪魔します (ojama shimasu) = I'll excuse myself for intruding. Said when entering someone's home or workspace. 邪魔 = nuisance/intrusion.

questions.question: What does 「気をつけて」(きをつけて) mean?
questions.explanation: 気をつけて (ki wo tsukete) = take care, be careful. 気をつける = to be careful/pay attention. 気 = spirit/attention, つける = to attach/pay.

questions.question: What does 「頑張って」(がんばって) mean?
options: Do your best / hang in there / good luck
questions.answer: Do your best / hang in there / good luck
questions.explanation: 頑張って (ganbatte) = do your best! / hang in there! / go for it! 頑張る = to do one's best, to persist. Often said before exams or challenges.

questions.question: What is 「兄」(あに)?
questions.explanation: 兄 (あに / ani) = my own older brother (humble/in-group form). お兄さん (おにいさん) = someone else's older brother or polite address. 弟 (おとうと) = younger brother.

questions.question: What is 「姉」(あね)?
questions.explanation: 姉 (あね / ane) = my own older sister (humble form). お姉さん (おねえさん) = someone else's older sister or polite address. 妹 (いもうと) = younger sister.

questions.question: What is 「祖父」(そふ)?
questions.explanation: 祖父 (そふ / sofu) = my grandfather (humble/in-group). おじいさん = someone else's grandfather or polite address. 祖母 (そぼ) = grandmother.

questions.question: What is 「体育」(たいいく)?
questions.explanation: 体育 (たいいく / taiiku) = physical education, P.E. 体 = body, 育 = raise/develop. 体育館 (たいいくかん) = gymnasium.

questions.question: What is 「理科」(りか)?
questions.explanation: 理科 (りか / rika) = science (as a school subject). 理 = reason/principle, 科 = subject/department. 理科の実験 = science experiment.

questions.question: What is 「水泳」(すいえい)?
questions.explanation: 水泳 (すいえい / suiei) = swimming. 水 = water, 泳 = swim. 水泳する = to swim (as a sport). 泳ぐ (およぐ) = to swim (the action).

questions.question: What is 「野球」(やきゅう)?
